scope: Synthetic two-task decodability assay using passive readers of shared 64-us tissue trajectories; numerical and assay-integrity qualification, with task success reported separately.
cue: Transient Kv1p5 channel inhibition at one of two source cells, with equal area-integrated inhibition and equal 8-us pulse duration; timing-only distributes that inhibition across both source cells.

reader.features: Area-weighted voltage in seven fixed cell IDs at three post-cue completed times; shared 21-dimensional support for both tasks. Also report final-time-only and 1-uV margin sensitivity.
reader.calibration: Fixed class means, no feature selection, normalization fit, hyperparameter search, or retraining on held-out data. Separate calibration in each physical arm.
reader.holdout: Four leave-one-location/timing-combination-out folds; each also withholds both held-out cue strengths. Single-task arms use unique physical inputs only, deduplicating the unused task label.

scope_exclusions: Not a biological measurement, causal use by a modelled consumer, feedback, polycomputing demonstration, or reconstruction/heredity result.
No new native mixed-intervention equivalence claim; simulation uses the unchanged qualified runtime, with new declared synthetic channel cues.
No independent biological replicates, population significance, novel geometries, stochastic noise calibration, or longer physical horizon.
The three-time reader has external post-cue buffering. Final-time-only reading is reported separately; neither establishes persistent memory or renewal.
The input-history baseline sees earlier raw controls, with the same 21-feature count and decoder class; it is an encoding baseline, not a tissue measurement.
Disconnecting gap junctions leaves extracellular/electrical routes and direct source-cell observations; chance performance is not required for this ablation.
Four folds are reported once without selecting the best fold. Shuffled calibration labels are descriptive nulls, not a significance claim.
Equal solver work and stable world IDs prepare independent-world distribution; no multi-GPU or throughput claim.
